current_disclosures.section: Products, Market, and Sales > Products by Business Unit and Market > Embedded Business Unit ("EBU")
current_disclosures.summary: The Embedded Business Unit (EBU) sells memory and storage products, including discrete/module DRAM, managed NAND, SSDs, and NOR, to intelligent edge devices in automotive, industrial, and consumer markets. The intelligent edge refers to connected systems where data analysis occurs close to the source, allowing AI-inference devices to operate self-contained without cloud connectivity.

comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded product portfolio and application scope
comparisons.peer_summary: The Embedded segment includes CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products addressing aerospace, defense, automotive, industrial, healthcare, communications, and other infrastructure markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose business segments targeting embedded markets, but they differ significantly in product composition and financial disclosure. MU’s Embedded Business Unit (EBU) focuses on memory and storage products (DRAM, NAND) and explicitly reports segment revenue ($4.61 billion in 2024). In contrast, AMD’s Embedded segment focuses on processing components (CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs) and does not provide specific revenue figures in this disclosure, focusing instead on the application scope (automotive, industrial, etc.).

sentences.text: EBU reported revenue of $4.61 billion 2024, $3.64 billion in 2023, and $5.24 billion in 2022.
EBU sales to the automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets in 2024 consisted primarily of LPDDR5 and LPDDR4 DRAM, DDR4 and DDR3 DRAM, and managed NAND.
The Embedded segment primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products.

Embedded products address computing needs in aerospace and defense, automotive, industrial, vision and healthcare, communications infrastructure, test measurement, emulation and prototyping, audio, video and broadcasting, and data center.
